subject: Aurora Analytics — MSA addendum + order form billing cycle and capacity lift
messages:
From: Emily White <emily.white@auroraanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@auroraanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal redlines + billing cadence question

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the renewal draft. I attached Aurora's redlines to the MSA (Aurora_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) and the updated order form showing the capacity uplift we discussed. A couple of quick items we need clarified before we can route to our procurement team:

- Billing cadence: Aurora prefers annual invoicing for enterprise customers; your draft still has quarterly billing. Can Redwood confirm whether an annual billing option is supported and if there are any implications for early termination fees?
- Change in scope: We want the order form to explicitly call out the 30% capacity uplift (line items in the attached spreadsheet). Please confirm any impact to SLA credits and per-token pricing for overages.
- Indemnity and data residency: Legal asked for a brief side letter on data residency commitments for EU users (we have a small EU subset). We can accept Redwood's standard addendum, but would like to see the language inserted under Section 7.

Can you loop in the appropriate folks on your side? We'd like to finalize this by EOD next Tuesday so procurement can process payment within their quarter.

Thanks — Emily
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurora Analytics

Subject: Re: Renewal redlines + billing cadence question

Emily —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear asks. Looping in Lauren from Legal and Ben from Renewals so we can consolidate answers and propose clean edits. High level answers up front:

1) Annual billing: Yes, we support annual invoicing. There is a billing-cycle mapping: annual prepay provides a 7% contract-level credit vs quarterly (I will let Lauren confirm language and any change to termination math).
2) Capacity uplift pricing: Ben, can you confirm the per-token uplift tiers for the +30% uplift and whether the customer stays on the same list price for baseline?
3) Data residency side letter: Lauren, please review Emily's requested insertion under Section 7 and advise whether Redwood's standard addendum is sufficient or if legal needs any additional guarantees.

Emily — we'll get a consolidated redline back by Monday EOD at the latest; if that works for procurement timeline we can aim for DocuSign by Tuesday. If you need earlier, tell me and we'll accelerate.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Renewal redlines + billing cadence question

Hi all —

Thanks for the note and attachments, Emily. I reviewed Aurora's PDF redlines and the order form. Below are proposed positions and the redline approach we'll take in the consolidated MSA/Order Form:

1) Billing cadence / early termination math
- We can accept annual prepayment and will reflect it on the order form as an invoicing option.
- Early termination: for annual prepay we propose a pro-rata refund of unused months less a 10% administrative fee. This is standard for prepay arrangements; Aurora's procurement asked whether there is a waiver for strategic customers — we'll accept a 5% admin fee if Aurora signs a 24-month minimum term.

2) Capacity uplift and pricing
- Ben confirmed the uplift pricing: baseline remains at current list; the +30% uplift will be priced at a blended uplift rate of -4% to the list for the uplift portion only. We will enumerate line items in the order form and include an overage metric (tokens) and a 14-day grace period before overage charges kick in.

3) SLA credit interaction
- SLA credits for availability apply to baseline and uplift equally; overage charges are separate chargeable events. We will add a short note in the coverage schedule tying credits to monthly availability targets.

4) Indemnity and data residency / side letter
- The requested insertion under Section 7 is acceptable if the side letter limits scope to Aurora's EU workload and references Redwood's standard EU Data Residency Addendum (attached as a doc link). We will not accept additional indemnities beyond existing Section 9 framework; for any deviation we will require a mutual cap tied to fees.

5) Minor language edits
- We'll accept most of Aurora's non-substantive edits. There are three spots where we want different wording (termination for convenience, export compliance clause, and notice addresses). I'll mark those in the redline PDF.

Next steps: I'll prepare a consolidated MSA/Order Form redline (tracked PDF) and a short cover memo summarizing the billing math and uplift pricing. Sean/Ben — can you confirm the pricing table Ben referenced so I can populate the order form? Emily — if the 24-month minimum term is not workable, flag that and we'll revert to 12-month with the 10% admin fee.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_EU_Data_Residency_Addendum.pdf (pdf, 24KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Final: consolidated redline next steps and ask for procurement

Emily —

Thank you. Per Lauren and Ben's input above, here's what we'll deliver by Monday EOD:

- Consolidated MSA with tracked changes reflecting the billing cadence language and the limited side letter language for EU data residency.
- Updated order form spreadsheet with explicit uplift line items and the blended uplift pricing for the +30% capacity.
- Short cover memo (1 page) that summarizes early termination math under annual prepay vs quarterly, and the proposed 24-month concession if Aurora prefers the 5% admin fee waiver.
- DocuSign envelope ready once Aurora confirms billing cadence and the minimum term preference.

Action for Aurora Procurement: please confirm by Monday 9am PT whether you: (a) want annual prepay with the 10% admin fee on early termination, (b) accept a 24-month minimum for the 5% admin fee waiver, or (c) prefer quarterly billing (no admin fee). That will let us finalize the DocuSign package for a Tuesday sign-off.

Appreciate the partnership — we'll be in touch with the redline artifacts.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
